title: Microsoft Sentinel Automation: Automation Rules and Playbooks

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)
Create and configure automation rules in Microsoft Sentinel; create and configure Microsoft Sentinel playbooks
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

html:
1Automation rules

An automation rule is a centralized, rule-based way to handle incidents and alerts without code. It has a trigger, conditions and actions.

Part Options
Triggers When incident is created, When incident is updated, When alert is created (alert trigger only for Scheduled, NRT and Microsoft security analytics rules)
Conditions equals / does not equal, contains, starts with, ends with (and their negations); the update trigger adds changed, changed from, changed to, added
Actions Add task, change status (closing reason and comment when closing), change severity, assign owner, add tag, run playbook

The condition Updated by can be Application, User, AIR, Alert grouping, Playbook, Automation rule or Other. Tag conditions can match any individual tag or the collection of all tags.

Exam tip

. Use automation rules for simple, high-volume tasks (assign, tag, close, set severity). Use a playbook only when you need an external system or logic.

2Order and timing

Rule Detail
Order number Sets execution order; lowest runs first
Queues Each trigger type has its own queue; created-trigger rules run before updated-trigger rules
Same number Rules with equal order run in random order; the portal does not stop duplicates
Actions inside a rule Run in the listed order
Playbook wait Under 1 s: the next action runs at once; under 2 min: next action within 2 min of the start; longer: next action at 2 min
Expiration date The rule is disabled after that date; ideal for penetration test noise
Exam tip

. Use an expiration date for a temporary rule, for example closing incidents from a scheduled penetration test. It turns itself off.

3Where automation rules are created

Place Note
Automation page > Automation rules tab Main place; in the Defender portal under Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > Automation
Analytics rule wizard > Automated response tab Bound to that analytics rule
Incidents page Pre-filled from an incident; suggests suppression and expiration (Azure portal only)

Rules can be exported and imported as ARM JSON.

In the Defender portal, alert-trigger rules act on Sentinel alerts; Microsoft incident creation rules are not supported; changes within 5 to 10 minutes are batched into one update, and an incident from Defender can take up to 10 minutes to reach a rule.

4Playbooks

A playbook is a collection of steps built on Azure Logic Apps, either Consumption or Standard (extra charges apply). Automation rules can run both types.

Trigger (Sentinel connector) Use
Microsoft Sentinel incident Recommended; receives the incident with its alerts and entities; attach it to an automation rule
Microsoft Sentinel alert (preview) Manual runs on alerts, or rules that create no incidents
Microsoft Sentinel entity Manual runs on an entity during an investigation or hunt

Common actions: Get incident, Update incident (status, owner, tags, severity, title, description), Add comment to incident, and Entities actions (get IP, host, account, URL, file hash). Updating needs the incident ARM ID.

Manual runs on alerts and on entities are not supported in the Defender portal.

5Permissions

Who or what Role
Sentinel service account that runs playbooks from an automation rule Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group; granting it needs Owner (portal link Manage playbook permissions)
Analyst who runs a playbook manually Microsoft Sentinel Responder (open the incident) plus Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
Engineer who attaches a playbook to a rule Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
Person who edits a playbook Logic App Contributor (Standard: Logic Apps Standard Contributor or Developer)
Person who may only enable or disable Logic App Operator

6Authenticating a playbook to Sentinel

Method Detail
Managed identity Enable system-assigned identity on the Logic App, then assign it a role on the workspace: Microsoft Sentinel Responder to update incidents, Reader to only receive them
Service principal Entra app; client ID, tenant and secret; Microsoft Sentinel Contributor to write, Reader to read
Entra user Signs in with a user account

Assigning roles needs Owner or User Access Administrator.

Exam tip

. Read or trigger = Reader. Write (update incident, add comment) = Responder or Contributor. Prefer a managed identity over a secret.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A SOC wants every incident created by one specific analytics rule to be assigned to the Tier 1 group automatically, with no code. What should be built?

  • AA playbook that calls an email connector for each alert
  • BAn automation rule triggered on incident creation that assigns an owner
  • CA workbook that lists incidents for the Tier 1 analysts
  • DA custom detection rule in Defender XDR for that alert
Show the answer

Answer: B. An automation rule with the incident created trigger can filter by analytics rule and assign an owner.

S2An automation rule must run a playbook, but the run is denied. What is the most likely missing permission?

  • AMicrosoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook resource group
  • BGlobal Administrator on the whole Microsoft Entra tenant
  • CWorkbook Contributor on the resource group of the workspace
  • DSecurity Operator in Microsoft Entra on the Sentinel workspace
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Sentinel service account needs Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group, and Owner is needed to grant it.

S3A company runs a two-week penetration test that will create many incidents. The SOC wants them closed automatically and the rule to stop after the test. Which setting helps?

  • AA lower order number so the rule runs before every other rule
  • BAn expiration date on an automation rule that closes the incidents
  • CA playbook that deletes the incidents once the test has ended
  • DAn analytics rule that is turned off for the full two weeks
Show the answer

Answer: B. An automation rule with an expiration date disables itself after that date.

S4Two automation rules use the incident created trigger with order numbers 10 and 20. A third uses the incident updated trigger with order 1. Which statement is correct?

  • AThe rule with order 1 runs first because it has the lowest number
  • BThe rule with order 20 runs first because it was created last
  • CThe created-trigger rules run first, in order 10 and then 20
  • DThe three rules run at random because the triggers differ
Show the answer

Answer: C. Each trigger type has its own queue, and created-trigger rules run before updated-trigger rules.

S5A playbook that uses a system-assigned managed identity must update the status of incidents. Which role should be assigned to the identity on the workspace?

  • AMicrosoft Sentinel Reader, which only reads incidents
  • BLogic App Operator, which can enable or disable the Logic App
  • CMicrosoft Sentinel Responder, which can update incidents
  • DPlaybook Operator, which can run playbooks manually
Show the answer

Answer: C. Updating incidents needs Responder (or Contributor); Reader only receives incidents.

S6A junior analyst must open incidents and run playbooks manually, with the least privilege. Which roles should be assigned?

  • AMicrosoft Sentinel Contributor on the whole subscription
  • BMicrosoft Sentinel Reader only, with Owner on the playbook
  • CLogic App Contributor only, on the resource group
  • DMicrosoft Sentinel Responder and Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
Show the answer

Answer: D. Responder opens the incident and Playbook Operator runs the playbook manually.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Which Sentinel trigger is recommended for playbooks?

Show the answer

Microsoft Sentinel incident.

R2Which service are playbooks built on?

Show the answer

Azure Logic Apps (Consumption or Standard).

R3Which role lets Sentinel run playbooks from automation rules?

Show the answer

Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor, on the playbook's resource group.

R4Which automation rules run first?

Show the answer

Created-trigger rules, before updated-trigger rules, lowest order number first.

R5Which action sets a closing reason?

Show the answer

Change status.

R6Where is the Sentinel automation page in the Defender portal?

Show the answer

Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration > Automation.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Automation rule trigger, conditions, actions; order number; expiration date
Triggers incident created, incident updated, alert created
Actions add task, change status, change severity, assign owner, add tag, run playbook
Playbook Logic Apps; incident trigger recommended
Run from rule Automation Contributor on the playbook resource group (Owner grants it)
Manual run Responder plus Playbook Operator
Playbook identity Reader to receive, Responder or Contributor to write
